A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LUNA and are readable, including their figures, tables and equations. V1 includes implementation and experimental appendices; v2 ends after the references. This omission is an observable version difference, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction, cross-identity driving, motion-quality and ablation results in Tables 1–4, plus an AvatarHQ evaluation in appendix Table 5.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical results in Tables 1–4 and their associated qualitative figures, despite omitting the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The canonical identity encoder, global/local neural animator and hybrid supervision remain unchanged in Section 3. Removing the appendix's implementation specifications does not establish a change to the underlying algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: V2 removes the AvatarHQ novel-view reconstruction evaluation using front-camera inputs. The training sources and evaluations involving Cloth10K, iPhone1K, NeuMan and Dome remain. Removing additional NeuMan examples does not remove NeuMan coverage.

E2.justification: The omitted AvatarHQ comparison evaluated ExAvatar, LSAvatar, DressRecon and ReLoo against LUNA. LSAvatar, DressRecon and ReLoo have no remaining evaluated comparisons in v2; ExAvatar remains in the main experiments. Comparator membership in Tables 1–4 is unchanged.

E3.justification: The removed AvatarHQ experiment compared subject-specific fitting from front-camera videos with LUNA using four front-view frames. V2 also omits the supplementary NeuMan procedure using manually selected viewpoint-covering references and every frame as a driver. Retained experiments have unchanged stated splits, metrics and training budgets.

E4.justification: V2 removes the appendix pose-accuracy case study and Figure 9, which examine hand-position and stepping-angle discrepancies caused by intermediate pose estimation. The main component ablations, trajectory analysis and challenging-pose cases remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates for the experimental results. The removed appendix does not contain such reporting.

E6.justification: V2 removes Table 5, including LUNA's AvatarHQ PSNR/L1/LPIPS of 21.85/0.031/0.131 and comparisons showing lower PSNR than DressRecon (22.18) and ReLoo (22.05). Additional qualitative results in Figures 9–10 disappear. All numerical results in Tables 1–4 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The appendix's explicit attention-update definitions and pose-conditioned teacher residual mapping, Equations 13–17, are omitted, along with the teacher's residual-composition formulas. The main formulation in Equations 1–12 remains unchanged; neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about direct 2D-driven, LBS-free 3D animation, disentangled deformation, hybrid supervision and zero-shot cross-identity generalization. Appendix removal does not revise these claims.

C2.justification: V2 loses the appendix explanation that corrupting driver texture through augmentation prevents identity leakage and encourages extraction of kinematic cues for cross-identity animation. Main interpretations and the limitations concerning occlusion, extreme poses and body-shape mismatch remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Removing Section 7 eliminates extensive implementation specifications: eight transformer layers and 16 attention heads, decoder construction and 65,536-Gaussian output, detached teacher targets, input/rendering resolutions, frame/view sampling, translation scaling and driving-image augmentations. These details are not relocated. Section 4.1 still points to the now-absent appendix, although its main hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds Large-scale Codec Avatars to the feed-forward reconstruction discussion and bibliography. References to ReLoo, Locality Sensitive Avatars from Video and DressRecon disappear with the appendix comparison. The broader positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 removes the appendix structure and its implementation and additional-experiment sections, but leaves the main narrative and section order essentially unchanged. Citation numbering and the version stamp change, while the unresolved appendix pointer remains.

P2.justification: Appendix Table 5 and Figures 9–10 are removed. Figures 1–8 retain identical image content and placement, and Tables 1–4 retain their structures. Other visual differences mainly involve citation numbering and reference-list reflow.

improvement.justification: Although the core method and main results remain intact, v2 substantially weakens reproducibility by removing the detailed architecture, decoder, sampling, resolution and augmentation specifications without replacement. It still directs readers to the absent appendix. Losing the AvatarHQ comparisons and additional qualitative evidence further reduces evaluability; the limited citation addition does not offset these losses.
